OTHER TIES: NAMED IN A CASE, PRINTS ITS MONEY, AUDITS OR MANAGES FUNDS (CENTRAL BANK OF THE COMOROS (COMOROS))
Source says: Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros). Ikililou Dhoinine is named in a documented case involving the Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros). The Comorian parliament's commission of inquiry into the economic citizenship programme reported in December 2017 that, according to his own collaborators, President Ikililou Dhoinine ordered that from January 2015 until the end of his term the programme's funds no longer be paid into the Banque Centrale des Comores, and that he could not explain what became of them. The commission concluded that he was therefore suspected of embezzling public money. Rapport de la Commission d'enquete parlementaire sur la loi relative a la citoyennete economique (Assemblee de l'Union des Comores)

Diario El Mundo reported that Nicolás Martínez, president of the Banco Central de Reserva, answered a summons from a Legislative Assembly commission investigating the debt the government had taken on and how it was used during the COVID-19 pandemic, and resigned the day after appearing. Deputies asked him whether the release of banks' liquidity reserve was designed so banks could buy Treasury paper; he answered that it was an autonomous decision of the banks. Source says: National Bank of Tajikistan (Tajikistan). Majlisi Namoyandagon of the Majlisi Oli of Tajikistan appoints or directs the board of the National Bank of Tajikistan (Tajikistan). The Law of the Republic of Tajikistan “On the National Bank of Tajikistan”, No. 722 of 28 June 2011, signed by President Emomali Rahmon, puts every seat on the bank's Board in the President's hands. Article 74(4) says the Chairman of the National Bank and his deputies are appointed to office and released from office by decree of the President, with the decrees submitted to the lower house of parliament for approval, and article 74(3) says the Board's three independent members are approved by the President on the Chairman's proposal. n:Ministry of Economy and Foreign Trade.box:

Ministry of Economy and Foreign Trade of Syria

Damascus, Syria

1 central bank tied to it.

OWNS SHARES OR SITS IN ITS GOVERNANCE (CENTRAL BANK OF SYRIA (SYRIA))
Source says: Central Bank of Syria (Syria). Ministry of Economy and Foreign Trade of Syria appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of Syria (Syria). Syria's Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued in Damascus on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, places the bank and its policy-making council under the government. Article 1 says the Monetary and Credit Council works within the general economic directions of the state approved by the Council of Ministers, and sets monetary policy in line with the state's general strategy. Article 8(3) says the Council's decisions are communicated to the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade, who may suspend for up to seven days any decision he considers contrary to the interest of the state, and if the disagreement continues he must refer the matter to the Council of Ministers to decide. Article 69 says the Governor is appointed, and his service terminated, by decree; article 2 puts the Council's non-bank seats, among them assistant ministers of economy, finance, agriculture and industry and the head of the State Planning Authority, in the gift of a decree on their ministries' proposal; and article 71 says the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade names the four supervising directors who sit with the Governor on the management committee. قانون النقد الأساسي — القانون رقم 23 لعام 2002 (Central Bank of Syria)

OWNS SHARES OR SITS IN ITS GOVERNANCE (CENTRAL BANK OF ARUBA (ARUBA))
Source says: Central Bank of Aruba (Aruba). Ministry of Finance of Aruba appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of Aruba (Aruba). Aruba's Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), as amended through AB 2014 no. 5 and published by the Centrale Bank van Aruba in Dutch and in the bank's English translation, keeps the bank under the Governor of Aruba and the Minister of Finance. Section 18 says the president and executive directors are appointed by the Governor from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board, and that the Governor may suspend or dismiss them by state decree. Section 19(3) says general guidelines for the performance of the duties of the president and executive directors can be set out in a state decree. Section 23 says the chairman of the Supervisory Board is the Government Commissioner, appointed and dismissed by the Governor, that the other supervisory directors are appointed by the Governor, and that they may be suspended or dismissed before the end of their term by the Governor. Section 27(1) says the Government Commissioner supervises the bank's activities on behalf of the Country and acts in accordance with general or specific instructions given by the Minister. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), English translation (Centrale Bank van Aruba)

OWNS SHARES OR SITS IN ITS GOVERNANCE (BERMUDA MONETARY AUTHORITY (BERMUDA))
Source says: Bermuda Monetary Authority (Bermuda). Ministry of Finance of Bermuda appoints or directs the board of Bermuda Monetary Authority (Bermuda). Bermuda's monetary authority is run by a board the finance minister appoints and can be told what to do by him. The Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 (1969:57), in the consolidated text the Authority publishes, says at section 21(2) that the Minister may give the Authority written general directions that appear to him necessary in the public interest, and that the Authority shall act in accordance with them. Section 4(1)(d) says eleven members of the Board are appointed by the Minister, section 4E(1) says the Minister appoints the Chairman, and section 4E(6) lets the Minister terminate the Chairman's appointment if satisfied he is unable or unfit to discharge his functions. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 (Bermuda Monetary Authority)

Source says: Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Solomon Islands). Ministry of Finance of Solomon Islands appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Solomon Islands). Under the Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012, which the bank publishes, section 37 says the Minister for Finance may, with the approval of Cabinet, give the Central Bank written directions where the Minister is of the opinion that coordination of monetary and fiscal policies or the public interest requires it, and must publish those directions in the Gazette and lay them before Parliament. Section 41(3) says the other directors of the Board are appointed by the Minister after consultation with the Governor, and section 41(1) says the Governor is appointed by the Governor-General on Cabinet's recommendation. Under section 44 the Governor, Deputy Governor and other Board members may be removed before their term ends only on grounds of permanent incapacity or serious misconduct, and the Governor only on a tribunal's recommendation. The Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Amendment) Act 2023 does not amend sections 37, 41 or 44. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012 (Central Bank of Solomon Islands)

Source says: Central Bank of Timor-Leste (Timor-Leste). Ministry of Finance of Timor-Leste is named in a documented case involving the Central Bank of Timor-Leste (Timor-Leste). In its report and opinion on the 2019 General State Account, Timor-Leste's Court of Accounts found that 6.6 million US dollars of European Union direct budget support, held in three bank accounts at the Banco Central de Timor-Leste, was not booked as state revenue, so 2019 state revenue was understated by that amount, and the 2.3 million US dollars spent from those accounts was spent outside the state budget and the General State Account. The report also recorded a closing accounting balance of 4.4 million US dollars against a cash balance at the central bank of 5.2 million US dollars. Source says: National Reserve Bank of Tonga (Tonga). Ministry of Finance of Tonga appoints or directs the board of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga (Tonga). The National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition, puts the bank's board in the government's hands and gives Cabinet the last word on policy disputes. Section 10(1) says the Minister, with the consent of Cabinet, appoints five directors and appoints the Chairman and Deputy Chairman; section 11(1) says the Governor is appointed by Cabinet on the Minister's recommendation; and section 11(3) says the Governor may be removed from office by Cabinet, on the Minister's recommendation made at the Board's request, for permanent incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties. Section 50(1) says the Minister may, with the consent of Cabinet, issue the bank written directives, and section 50(4) says that where the Minister and the Board disagree about a policy the Board has determined, the Minister must submit the disagreement to Cabinet to determine the policy to be adopted by the bank. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, CAP. 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition (Attorney General's Office, Tonga)

Source says: Central Bank of Aruba (Aruba). Stichting Fondo Desaroyo Aruba is named in a documented case involving the Central Bank of Aruba (Aruba). Aruba's General Audit Chamber, reviewing the country's 2001-2004 annual accounts, found that contributions paid into an earmarked account held at the Centrale Bank van Aruba in the country's name for the Fondo Desaroyo Aruba foundation were not accounted for completely, correctly and on time. Of a balance of 19.3 million Aruban florins at the end of 2000, only the 3 million paid in by Aruba appeared in the country's accounts, while 16,898,503 florins paid in by the Netherlands were left off the balance sheet. Onderzoek naar de jaarrekeningen Land 2001-2004 (Algemene Rekenkamer Aruba)
